slot.brief: A temperature has a specific numerical reading that is equal (or in a given ratio) on two non-standard thermometers (e.g. X and Celsius); use the linear relation between scales to find the reading.

stem: A thermometer X reads $10$ °X at $0$ °C and $160$ °X at $100$ °C. At what Celsius temperature do the two thermometers show the same numerical reading?

verdicts.working: The X reading is X = 10 + 1.5C. Equating X = C gives C = -20 °C.

working:
$X=1.5C+10$; setting $X=C$ gives $C=-20$ °C.

Independent check: The X reading is X = 10 + 1.5C. Equating X = C gives C = -20 °C.
solution:
The thermometer scale is linear, so $X=10+\frac{160-10}{100}C=10+1.5C$.
Setting the readings equal, $X=C$:
$$C=10+1.5C\implies C=-20^\circ\text{C}.$$
